description_en: Digital Business Models is a required specialist course in Business Administration and Marketing. In an era shaped by continuous technological innovation, business professionals and leaders need the knowledge and skills to adapt and succeed in the digital economy. The widespread use of the Internet has placed business models at the center of strategy and management, while the digitalization of business processes continues to transform corporate practices. This course provides a structured conceptual approach to the common features and distinctive characteristics of digital business models. It introduces the core B2C-4C-Net and B2B-4S-Net models and develops an integrated strategic perspective on information technology, management, financial technology, digital transformation, business model design, and innovation.

This course equips students in economics and business with practical knowledge and management skills for organizational settings. Its main topics are: • Effective management in a changing world. • Principles of effective management. • Meeting and reporting skills. • Budget and time management. • Conflict management. • Personal stress management. • Problem-solving and decision-making skills.

Customer behavior research is essential for identifying consumer needs, selecting appropriate target segments, positioning products and brands, and developing effective marketing and business strategies. The course examines both purchasing and post-purchase behavior, including customer retention, loyalty, and repeat purchasing. Students practice analytical reasoning, critical discussion, questioning, and the analysis of real business situations. They learn to identify and evaluate customer psychology and behavior, conduct behavior research for specific brands, products, or services, and apply the findings to positioning, segmentation, and marketing planning. The course supports students pursuing customer research, market research, brand management, and broader marketing management roles.

Advanced Microeconomics extends the foundations of introductory microeconomics through seven major topics: • The efficiency of competitive markets. • Applications of consumer choice theory to economic behavior and policy. • Price discrimination and pricing under market power. • Game theory and strategic decisions that account for competitors' reactions. • General equilibrium and interactions among related markets. • Asymmetric information. • Externalities and public goods. The course emphasizes both the theoretical conditions behind these concepts and their application to real markets such as telecommunications, electricity, and aviation.

Advanced Macroeconomics is a specialist course in the Economics program. It provides in-depth knowledge of macroeconomic policies and policy instruments, their effects on major economic objectives, and their implications for business activity and people's lives.

Cryptocurrency Technology and Electronic Payment Systems provides foundational knowledge of cryptocurrencies and digital payment systems in the modern economy, drawing on reliable academic and institutional sources. The course explains what cryptocurrencies are, why they represent an innovative form of money and digital assets, and how they operate within blockchain ecosystems. Its main topics are: • The second era of the Internet. • Introduction to cryptocurrencies. • Cryptocurrencies as an asset class. • Blockchain ecosystems. • Central bank digital currencies. • Introduction to financial technology and Big Tech in finance. • Electronic payment systems. • Credit card innovation. • Electronic commerce.

This course equips students with the knowledge required to understand accounting operations in Vietnamese banks. Upon completion, students will have a comprehensive view of how accounting is organized and performed in credit institutions and commercial banks. Core topics include cash transactions, deposit mobilization, lending operations, interbank and customer payments, international payments and foreign-exchange trading, securities investment and trading, revenue and expense accounting, and bank financial statements.

Advanced Commercial Banking is a required specialist course for Banking and Finance students. It provides in-depth knowledge of commercial banking operations, including deposit mobilization, personal lending, corporate credit and trade finance, international payments, foreign-exchange operations, digital transformation, and modern banking trends. The course also develops professional skills and the ability to apply theory when resolving practical situations in commercial bank operations.

Money and Banking is a required foundation course for Banking and Finance students. It combines theoretical and practical perspectives on monetary systems, central bank operations, the banking system, the role of central banks, and the instruments used to implement monetary policy. These foundations prepare students for more advanced courses in banking and finance.

This course equips learners with essential digital competencies for effective university study and sustainable career development in the digital era. It combines theoretical foundations in information management, responsible technology use, online collaboration, digital thinking, digital security and ethics, and creative digital content production. Students practice solving real academic and professional problems using modern digital tools and mindsets. The course aligns with the Digital Competency Framework for Learners in Higher Education, supporting foundational digital competency and lifelong learning. It also develops critical thinking, collaboration, creativity, and the effective use of information and communication technology.

Graphic and Multimedia Design provides essential knowledge of design rules, visual principles, image composition, color, and typography for creating advertising materials and brand identity products. Beyond two-dimensional graphics, students study visual motion, special effects, script development, storyboarding, and the editing of promotional and event videos for business communication.

This course introduces the foundations of electronic commerce and the issues involved in developing e-commerce systems and business plans. Its main topics are: • Characteristics of e-commerce and digital business models. • Basic information technology infrastructure. • E-commerce presence and channel development. • Security and electronic payment issues. • Electronic marketing. • Ethical and social issues in electronic commerce.

Company Law provides students with foundational knowledge of business organizations and the principal legal issues affecting enterprises, including their formation, legal status, governance, and internal business relationships.

International Tax Law provides students with knowledge of Vietnamese tax law and policy as applied to foreign individuals and organizations operating in Vietnam. The course focuses particularly on the avoidance of double taxation and the prevention and control of transfer pricing.

Insurance Business Law covers the theoretical foundations and current legal framework governing insurance business and insurance contracts. Topics include the legal status of insurance business entities; key terminology in insurance law; the concept, characteristics, and classification of insurance contracts; contract content and form; life insurance, property and damage insurance, and civil liability insurance; and the resolution of disputes arising from insurance contracts.

This course introduces the core concepts of statistics for business administration and marketing and explains how businesses, nonprofit organizations, and governments use data to understand problems and make better decisions. Applications span operations, marketing, finance, strategic planning, and other management functions. Students develop knowledge and skills in: • Collecting, analyzing, and presenting data. • Testing hypotheses. • Applying common econometric models. • Designing marketing and business research. • Preparing and presenting research reports. The ability to make timely, accurate, and profitable data-informed decisions is emphasized as an important strategic advantage.
